title: Uniform Event-Time Confidence Bands for Low-Rank Panels with Data Missing Not at Random
banked_reason: The headline proves a valid generic conditional transfer, but the event-transfer class does not imply the required high-probability nonlinear-remainder or feasible-score events.
gap_reasons: The note does not prove honest feasible growing-event-curve inference: its coverage theorem assumes vanishing nonlinear-remainder and feasible-score failure probabilities, while neither probability control follows from the stated event-transfer class.
Covariance consistency is likewise not established, because the theorem stops at a deterministic implication from an unproved score-discrepancy rate.
The sharp primitive remainder envelope, its counterarray, and the feasible-score stability needed for actual bands are all deferred to oeq:attainable-remainder-frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived exact eventwise aggregation, overlap-aware covariance bookkeeping, a singular-covariance-safe log^5 Gaussian approximation, and a generic finite-error multiplier transfer, with all five cited inputs verified from official source text. The promised feasible field-tier band collapsed because the frozen event-transfer class supplies neither a vanishing simultaneous block-remainder failure probability nor stochastic feasible-score stability. A future re-raise must prove those rates—likely through signed second-order KKT and counterarray analysis—or openly add primitive assumptions; editorial wording and panel-sanity repairs alone cannot lift the result.
tldr: The note's exact-rank, row-heteroskedastic model is now explicitly an event-transfer class, not the published Choi--Yuan class.  The eligible blocks aggregate exactly into one event-by-cell score, and a generic remainder event \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) yields a finite whole-curve error contribution \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}+Cu\sqrt{\log(2p)}\).  Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike's 2022 singular-covariance-safe theorem sharpens the Gaussian component to log power five and gives the balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).  Feasible growing-curve coverage remains conditional on the displayed remainder-event and score-stability probabilities.  The published approximate-rank, i.i.d. homoskedastic selected-functional class and the event-transfer class are incomparable; their explicit balanced rank-one common subclass is nonempty, but the attained nonlinear-remainder frontier remains open.
gap: Published low-rank MNAR results provide entrywise, scalar, or fixed block inference. Published staggered DiD results provide simultaneous event paths under parallel trends. Neither literature derives a growing adoption-aligned Choi--Yuan influence array, its shared-cell covariance, and a primitive feasible unit-heteroskedastic multiplier law.
fill: The exact block coefficients are aggregated into one event-by-cell map, the Choi--Yuan perturbation ratios are bounded at each finite \(n\) by fixed vanishing envelopes over a complete-array class, and each finite optimization uses an explicitly induced slice. Residual-square training is confined to \(\mathcal V_n\), all noise conditions hold on \(\mathcal Q_n^+=\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\cup\mathcal V_n\), and the feasible covariance and multiplier sums remain on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\). Gaussian approximation plus anti-concentration then yields honest whole-curve coverage. The open necessity node asks for the smaller attained remainder scale rather than declaring the coarse sufficient envelope sharp.
